question: Should OpenClaw accept default-on `openclaw.schema.json` sidecar refreshes and root `$schema` stamping during OpenClaw-owned config writes once this PR is merge-clean?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it changes persisted config-write output and creates a new operator-visible artifact, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Accept after rebase
options.body: Rebase or resolve conflicts against current main, keep include-backed roots preserving their root file, and accept the sidecar plus root `$schema` behavior as the default config-write contract.

options.title: Make it explicit
options.body: Ask for a command-driven or opt-in schema refresh path instead of changing every OpenClaw-owned config write by default.

options.title: Close in favor of manual export
options.body: Keep the existing `openclaw config schema` workflow and close the automatic sidecar direction if maintainers do not want another persisted artifact.

recommendation.title: Accept after rebase
recommendation.body: Rebase or resolve conflicts against current main, keep include-backed roots preserving their root file, and accept the sidecar plus root `$schema` behavior as the default config-write contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config-area history makes this the best available routing owner for config writer compatibility acceptance.
